Zirconia is a common coating material used for thermal barrier coatings in turbine engines.
Radiation becomes more significant as temperatures are raised for higher efficiency in advanced engines.
The two-flux method is used to provide a simplified approach for modeling the radiative heat transfer in the semitransparent thermal barrier coating.
A two-band approximation is used to model the spectral radiative properties of zirconia, with the band for large wavelengths (small frequencies) considered opaque.
The presence of a thin opaque soot layer on the exposed surface of the zirconia coating can increase the metal temperatures by absorbing the incident radiation.
For a clean zirconia coating, the high scattering of zirconia reflects away much of the incident radiation, leading to lower temperatures in the coating.
The relative positions of the temperature distributions for bare metal, opaque zirconia coating, and semitransparent zirconia coating are the same, regardless of external radiative heating.
The thickness of the zirconia coatings analyzed in the paper is 0.25 mm.
Radiative effects are relatively smaller for turbine blades compared to combustor liners due to the higher convective heat transfer coefficients.
Semitransparency is found to be beneficial in limited conditions where it increases the effective coating thermal conductivity for heating primarily by convection.
The iterative solution method used in the paper involves solving the two-flux equation for the radiative flux distribution and the heat conduction equation for the temperature distribution.
The Runge-Kutta numerical integration method is used to solve the two-flux equation for the radiative flux distribution within the semitransparent coating.

The absorption optical thickness of the zirconia coating is small, and the scattering albedo is close to one, which allows the shooting method to be used for solving the two-point boundary value problem.
The paper provides an analytical procedure for modeling the radiative heat transfer in semitransparent thermal barrier coatings using the two-flux method.
The results illustrate how the analysis can be used to examine the effect of semitransparency for various parameters in turbine engine thermal barrier coatings.
